A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MegaSynth work. All 17 pages, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments, training and data ablations, view-count analyses and qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains original reconstruction results and adds depth measurements, synthetic-dataset comparisons, a monocular-depth experiment and a user study.

M1.justification: The scene-generation pipeline, camera sampling, mixed-data training and rendering/geometry losses remain unchanged. Fine-tuning an existing Depth Anything V2 model extends the empirical application of MegaSynth without introducing a new proposed algorithmic component.

E1.justification: V2 adds Kubric and Front3D as synthetic training sources and extends evaluation to monocular depth estimation on Hypersim. The existing DL3DV, Hypersim, MipNeRF360 and Tanks & Temples reconstruction coverage remains.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained DL3DV-trained LRMs and optimization-based 3DGS, v2 evaluates GS-LRM trained with DL3DV plus Kubric or Front3D in Table 5. Table 6 also compares the original Depth Anything V2 model against its MegaSynth-tuned version, substantially expanding the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds AbsRel and δ1 evaluation of rendered Hypersim depth, specifies an eight-view, resolution-128 GS-LRM protocol for the new dataset comparison, evaluates monocular depth with ViT-B, and introduces human rankings of dataset properties. The original reconstruction splits, 32-input/32-target protocol and Appendix B training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The supporting analyses now test alternative synthetic training sources and human judgments of geometric difficulty and diversity. Conversely, v1's progressive geometry/material/lighting analysis in Table 5 is removed, and Table 4 loses the DL3DV-indoor comparison of all four training strategies. These removals are not restored in the appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new user study reports point rankings without an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds depth scores to Table 1 and results in Tables 5–7. For example, new Table 6 reports AbsRel/δ1 of 0.213/0.761 for Depth Anything V2 and 0.158/0.799 after MegaSynth tuning. V1's data-control results and distinct DL3DV-indoor MegaSynth-only/joint-training results disappear. Retained reconstruction scores and Figure 6's plotted values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the mathematical model description and losses remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, derivation or formal assumption is introduced; the added depth metrics serve empirical evaluation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the contribution claims to other tasks, specifically monocular depth estimation, and emphasize improved reconstructed geometry. The central synthesis contribution, 1.2–1.8 dB reconstruction gains and argument about limited reliance on semantics remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new comparisons as showing that realistic assets or scene composition do not guarantee useful reconstruction training, emphasizing geometric difficulty and diversity instead. It removes the old Table 5 interpretation of reconstruction scores as evidence of distribution alignment. Existing failure-case explanations and indoor/outdoor qualifications remain.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the monocular-depth backbone as ViT-B and specifies the SRT provenance of Kubric data, alongside brief dataset-size descriptions. Appendix A/B generation parameters, hyperparameters, hardware and training-time disclosures remain unchanged. Detailed procedures for the new depth experiment and user study are not supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to 3D-FRONT, Kubric, SRT and PointOdyssey, and explicitly positions MegaSynth against synthetic datasets using realistic assets or artist-designed scenes. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the introduction and Section 6.5, while Section 4's numbered Overview becomes an unnumbered paragraph. Several captions are shortened, but the main narrative organization and appendix prose remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds three main-text tables, removes the old data-control table, expands Table 1 and locally rearranges existing displays. Figure 5 loses one comparison pair. Figure 6 extends its vertical axis to 0–25 without changing plotted values. The overall layout and appendix visualizations remain intact.

improvement.justification: The new geometry measurements and direct synthetic-dataset comparisons strengthen validation, while the monocular-depth experiment demonstrates another use of MegaSynth. Benefits are limited by sparse documentation of the new studies and removal of earlier analyses; the referenced appendix alignment analysis is absent. With the method and headline reconstruction results unchanged, this is an incremental net improvement.
